approach: Build the drain fix-request work (not in this base) and answer both findings. pin.rs turns the checker's reported problems into SourceFinding values (study, file, kind, statement, evidence, anchor). The anchor names the study entry that holds the statement. Every string at any depth is credited to its nearest ancestor with an id, term or name (else its top-level key). A candidate matches the statement ONE way only: the candidate contains the statement, or the statement contains the candidate and the candidate covers at least half the statement's length (finding 2). No match, or more than three owners, gives a hash anchor. steward.rs builds one word-free marker 'Source fix: studies/<study>/<file> <kind> <anchor>', used as the request title and the lookup key, plus the request text through StewardRequest::new, and citing_request. drain.rs RealSteps::check_page queues one request per finding, skipping a finding whose request is open or whose marker was already queued in this run. The run set is a process static in drain.rs that is now ALSO carried across a rebuild re-exec: Carried gets a serde-default field source_fix_queued, run_pass stores the set into the carry file when it writes it and restores it from the carry it takes before the pass (finding 1). guarded already deletes the carry on a fresh start, so a fresh drain starts with an empty set. Pass/fail and the Check detail do not change. c45 is re-cited from the pinned source if it can be read, else at the two already-validated reopen quotes, with the CHANGELOG saying what was not checked. model.json and intro.json are verified by Grep and edited only for a leftover.

decisions.choice: Queue a marker at most once per drain RUN with a process static in drain.rs, `static SOURCE_FIX_QUEUED: Mutex<BTreeSet<(PathBuf, String)>>` keyed by `athena.git.dir()` and the marker, and hand it across the rebuild re-exec through the existing carry file. check_page checks and inserts under the lock before `Athena::queue` and removes the entry if queueing fails. `Carried` gets `#[serde(default)] pub source_fix_queued: Vec<(String, String)>` (directory, marker; the directory through to_string_lossy). `run_pass` (drain.rs:3303) does two things: after `take_carry` and before `pass()` it restores the carried pairs into the static; where it calls `store_carry(.., &Carried::from_report(&report))` it fills the field from the static (`Carried { source_fix_queued: queued_source_fixes(), ..Carried::from_report(&report) }`). `from_report`, `apply`, `store_carry`, `take_carry`, `guarded`, `follow_restart` and the Report are not changed. `guarded` (3842) already removes the carry unless the pid file names this process (a drain that replaced its own image), so only the continuing drain restores markers and a fresh drain starts empty.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. I read drain.rs 3197-3322 and commands.rs 319-358: after a landing that touches the build, `drain_concurrent` ends in Stop::Rebuilt, `run_pass` writes `drain.carry`, `follow_restart` execs the new binary, and the new process builds a fresh `RealSteps::live` and an empty static. A static alone therefore does not cover the whole run, as the critic says. The carry file is the existing run state that survives the re-exec and is cleared on a fresh start, so riding on it keeps one mechanism and needs no new file. A `#[serde(default)]` field keeps old carry files and the test literal `earlier_pass()` (tests/drain.rs:2188, uses `..Carried::default()`) valid. The fix's own landing is an outcome landing (drain.rs:1814, OUTCOME_PATHS 462), so Drain::rate (2432-2451) runs check_page right after it; with 'open only' dedup a landed-but-ineffective fix would be re-queued. A field on RealSteps would break about 40 struct literals including tests/job_plan.rs:173 and tests/focus.rs:159, which are not deliverables. The static is a Mutex like TABLE_LOCK (799), so concurrent workers under `drain_concurrent` are safe, and each test Fixture has its own directory, so tests in one process do not share keys. Known limit, stated in the doc comment and CHANGELOG: a drain killed or stopped and started again by hand is a new run and may queue the marker once more.

rejected.option: A static alone, taking process scope as run scope (the previous plan)
rejected.why: False after a rebuild re-exec: the new process starts with an empty set, so a landed fix whose contradiction remains would be queued again once per rebuild.

rejected.option: A new file in the state directory next to drain.carry, removed by guarded
rejected.why: A second state file needs its own write, read and clean-up paths and a race with the carry. The carry already has exactly the lifetime wanted (written before exec, taken by the continuing drain, removed by guarded on a fresh start).

rejected.option: Add the markers to Report and let Carried::from_report copy them
rejected.why: Report has many struct literals in tests and is printed as JSON; the markers are not part of the summary. run_pass reads the static directly, with no Report change.

rejected.option: A field on RealSteps or Athena
rejected.why: Every struct literal of RealSteps (tests/drain.rs, job_plan.rs, focus.rs) would need it; far larger than the goal, and a new RealSteps is built per pass anyway so it would not survive the re-exec.

rejected.option: Treat only an open request as a duplicate
rejected.why: The fix lands, the rating is met, check_page runs and the same finding is queued again.

rejected.option: Never queue a marker that ever had a request
rejected.why: A failed or abandoned fix would never be asked for again, and a regression after a landed fix would never be queued, even in a later run.

decisions.choice: finding_anchor walks the file's JSON passing an 'owner' down. An object's owner is its own `id`, else `term`, else `name`; otherwise it inherits the nearest ancestor's owner. A string with no owner takes its top-level key if made of [A-Za-z0-9._-] and at most 40 characters. An owner text that is not word-safe becomes 'n' plus 16 hex digits of the FNV-1a 64 of its normalised text. Every string value at any depth is a candidate except `id`, `term`, `name` values and `claims` arrays. Matching is ONE-WAY (answers finding 2): after lowercasing, whitespace collapse and trimming quote marks, a candidate matches when (a) it contains the statement and the statement is at least 12 characters, or (b) the statement contains the candidate, the candidate is at least 12 characters, and the candidate's length is at least half the statement's length. The anchor is the sorted, de-duplicated owner keys of all matches joined with '+', when there are one to three of them. With no match, a non-JSON file, or more than three owners, the anchor is 'h' plus 16 hex digits of FNV-1a 64 of the normalised statement. The rule goes in the doc comment.
decisions.reason: model.json keeps text in nested objects without an id (t2's retry.changes, model.json:28-30) and name-only entries (unhandled.failures, model.json:119); crediting descendants to the nearest owner covers them. The previous either-way rule with a 12-character floor let a short definition inside a long statement credit an unrelated entry and merge two contradictions into one stable but wrong anchor. The half-length rule keeps the real cases: the checker quoting a fragment of a longer entry (case a), or quoting the entry plus a little more (case b), while a short unrelated definition (under half) is not credited. More than three owners means the statement is broad, so the hash is used rather than an arbitrary prefix.

rejected.option: Either-way containment with a 12-character floor on the shorter side (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The critic's false positive: a short definition inside a long statement credits an unrelated entry.

rejected.option: Prefer the candidate whose owner the checker's evidence names
rejected.why: Evidence is model prose that changes between runs and mostly cites source paths, not study entries; it would make the key unstable.

rejected.option: Match only direct string fields of objects that have an id or term
rejected.why: Nested model.json texts and name-keyed failures would fall back to the hash and be queued again.

rejected.option: Key on the statement text or the evidence
rejected.why: The model rewrites both between runs, so the same contradiction would be queued again.

risks.risk: The model paraphrases a statement so it matches no study entry, or quotes a different set of entries next run. The anchor then changes and the same contradiction can be queued again in a later run.
risks.mitigation: Matching ignores case and spacing, accepts a candidate containing the statement or a statement containing a candidate that covers at least half of it, and reaches nested strings. Evidence is not in the key. Within one run (including across a rebuild, via the carry) the set holds the marker, not the contradiction, which bounds the cost. A miss costs one extra request in a later run, never a wrong pass or fail. The CHANGELOG states the limit.

risks.risk: The one-way half-length rule is stricter than before, so a checker statement that is a short fragment of a long entry (under half its length, and not contained in a candidate) falls back to the hash anchor, which is less stable between runs.
risks.mitigation: Case (a) keeps the common form (the checker quotes a fragment, so the candidate contains the statement) with no length limit beyond 12 characters on the statement. Only a statement that contains a smaller candidate needs the half-length coverage. A hash miss costs one extra request in a later run; the unit tests cover both directions.

risks.risk: A landed fix that did not remove the contradiction is asked for again by the next drain run (one request per run), because a landed request is closed and so not open.
risks.mitigation: Intended as a retry, limited to one per marker per run, including across rebuilds. The CHANGELOG says so. Blocking on 'ever landed' was rejected because it would hide a regression.

risks.risk: The process-wide set is hidden state, persists for the life of the process, and a test cannot reset it; the carry file adds a second place it is stored.
risks.mitigation: The key includes the repository directory and each test Fixture has its own directory. The set only grows by one entry per queued marker. The doc comment on the static says it is the run scope and names the carry. The carry field has a serde default, and guarded drops a stale carry on a fresh start (test source_fix_a_fresh_drain_ignores_a_stale_carry).

risks.risk: A drain that is stopped or killed (no exec) and started again by hand is a new run with an empty set and may queue a landed-but-ineffective marker once more.
risks.mitigation: This is the same as any fresh drain, matches how guarded treats the tallies, and costs one request per fresh run. Stated in the static's doc comment and the CHANGELOG.

risks.risk: The carry now holds directory paths; a non-UTF-8 repository path would not round-trip exactly.
risks.mitigation: The directory is stored with to_string_lossy as a String, so store_carry never fails on it; at worst the marker is not recognised after restore and one extra request is queued in the continuing process.

risks.risk: Existing drain tests that run the real check with a failing fake checker now commit request records, which could change commit counts or Records assertions.
risks.mitigation: The commit happens only when the fake reports a problem, and only inside RealSteps::check_page. `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test` (criteria 4 and 6) are the check; tests/drain.rs is a deliverable and any assertion the new commit breaks is updated there.

risks.risk: c45 cannot be matched to a line that says Queued in this environment, so the real source check may flag c45 and queue one fix request on the next drain.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG says plainly that the cited lines do not say Queued and that the pinned source was not read. The Host question asks for the mount. With the once-per-run set and the open-request skip, that finding yields at most one request per run.

risks.risk: Queueing fails (a boundary word in a study or file name, a redaction change, a records commit error) and would abort the check.
risks.mitigation: The anchor is word-free (an id/term/key restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-], or h/n plus hex). The run set entry is removed when the queue call fails. A build or queue error is appended to the check detail and never changes pass or fail.

risks.risk: The model-backed check against the real pin cannot run here, so 'the drain source check passes on the corrected study' is not shown.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 3's demonstration records the route the conventions test prints and does not claim the source check ran. The CHANGELOG states which part was not run.

demonstrations.method: New drain tests in tests/drain.rs, calling the production `RealSteps { athena, ui: &Quiet, page: &StubPage, lander }.check_page()` with a counting `SourceJudge` fake. Each builds its own claims.json through `commit_study` with its own files: c1 'Teardown closes a task, and a closed task can reopen.' and c2 'A worker slot is released when its pull request is ready.' (the shared Texts claims.json has only c1). Test 1 `source_fix_queues_one_request_per_contradiction_and_none_while_open`: run 1 reports one `contradicted` problem on claims.json whose statement is a fragment of c1's text with no id and evidence 'pinned-source/bin/x.sh lines 30-33'; run 2 reports the same fragment with different case and spacing and different evidence; run 3 reports that problem plus a c2 fragment. Expected: one job whose first line is `Source fix: studies/demo/claims.json contradicted c1` after runs 1 and 2, two after run 3, the second ending ` c2`; run 1's text has the statement, the defanged evidence, an `Acceptance:` section and `Files: studies/demo/claims.json`; `request_text_touches` is only that file; `steward::citing_request` returns the job; the Check is still failed with `demo/claims.json` and the statement in its detail; and the production `steps.queue()` lists the job in items and plan with no open question. Test 2 `source_fix_is_not_queued_again_after_its_job_lands_in_the_same_run`: after run 1, helper `close_request(fx, athena, job, OutcomeState::Landed)` commits an `AnyRecord::Outcome` (as seed_repeated_cause does, tests/drain.rs:4464-4519; Outcome fields as in tests/reconcile.rs:62-79); the fake still reports the contradiction; check_page again leaves exactly one request job, none open, and `steps.queue()` does not list it. Test 3 `source_fix_closed_without_landing_is_queued_by_a_later_run_only`: in a fresh fixture seed a request with `athena.queue(&source_fix_request(&finding))` (hand-built finding, anchor 'c1') and close it as Failed; the first check_page queues one new request (this process has not queued the marker for this directory); closing it and calling check_page again queues none. Test 4 `source_fix_process_failure_queues_nothing`: a 'did not report reading this file' problem queues nothing. For finding 1, Test 5 `source_fix_marker_is_carried_across_a_rebuild`: in a fresh fixture, run `drain::run_pass(root, &Quiet, || { real.check_page()...; drain::drain(&rebuilding stub, limits, &Quiet) }, &|_| { read drain::carry_file(root) with serde_json into drain::Carried; assert source_fix_queued holds (athena.git.dir(), marker); Ok(report of a second plain stub drain) })`; one request exists. Test 6 `source_fix_marker_in_the_carry_is_not_queued_again_after_the_restart`: in a fresh fixture whose directory this process has never queued for, `drain::store_carry(root, &Carried { source_fix_queued: vec![(dir, marker)], ..Carried::default() })`, then `drain::run_pass(root, ...)` whose pass runs check_page with the fake still reporting the contradiction; no request job exists afterwards (the marker can only have come from the carry file, since the static is empty for that directory). Test 7 `source_fix_a_fresh_drain_ignores_a_stale_carry`: `guarded` with a stale carry holding the marker (pid file not naming this process) removes the carry, so check_page queues one request. Test 8 `a_carry_without_the_field_still_reads`: an old carry JSON lacking `source_fix_queued` deserialises via take_carry. Core unit tests: pin.rs `source_finding_*` and steward.rs `source_fix_*`, including pin test `source_finding_a_short_unrelated_definition_is_not_credited` (a 20-character glossary definition contained in a 100-character statement, under half its length, is not an owner; the anchor is the real owner or the hash) and `source_finding_a_fragment_of_one_entry_is_credited` (candidate contains statement).
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain source_fix && cargo test -p athena-core source_f && cargo test -p athena-cli && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: One request after run 1, still one after run 2 although case, spacing and evidence changed and no id was named, two after run 3. No second request after the first job lands with the contradiction still reported. A failed request is re-queued by a later run only. steps.queue() lists the new job. The carry file holds the queued marker before the restart, and a marker restored from the carry is not queued again. A stale carry on a fresh start is dropped. The pin and steward unit tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without dedup, run 2 makes a second request. With a key of file and kind only, run 3's c2 is skipped (count 1). With a key on evidence or the raw statement, run 2 makes a second request. With 'open only' dedup, test 2 finds a second request. With no queueing, the count after run 1 is 0. With a raw marker, the unit test comparing it to the first line of the built request fails. With direct-fields-only matching, the nested-entry anchor test fails. With either-way containment, the short-definition test fails. With the static but no carry field, test 5 fails (carry lacks the marker) and test 6 queues a request.
